newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease in caution, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease in caution, off lows.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged lower on Monday amid caution prompted by upcoming parliamentary votes on corruption probes against deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, but recovered from lows on support, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 ended down one point, or 0.06 percent at 1,554, after rebounding from an early low of 1,516. Daily volume plunged to 18.87 trillion lira ($156.2 million) from Friday's 28.38 trillion ($236.8 million).

"Both sellers and buyers were weak. Political uneasiness is negatively affecting the market. The upcoming votes raised political uncertainty and this sentiment may persist until the weekend," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
Brokers said the index rebounded on support expected at the index's 1,500 mark.

Parliament will debate two corruption allegations against Ciller on Tuesday and another one on Wednesday. All probes were previously rejected by parliamentary commissions, but a vote in the general assembly will be final.
